title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical error on this page. (8) and (9) correctly describe the D_3h ≅ S_3 × Z/2 symmetry of the configuration, with S_3 acting by rotations and τ by the equatorial reflection.
Notational inconsistency: the index set is called J in (4)–(9), but (10) writes {R_i | i ∈ I}.

Next page (not this one): the blow-up at three points (Möbius bands glued in) has χ = −1, i.e. 3 crosscaps. Grothendieck's 'χ = 1−g, so genus 2' uses a nonstandard convention for non-orientable genus; it is not an error in χ.

ideas.what: Embedding S_3 × Z/2 into O(3) as the symmetry group of three equatorial points: rotations act by permutation on the plane and by sign on the polar axis; τ is the equatorial reflection, i.e. complex conjugation.
ideas.modern_name: Real/antiholomorphic automorphisms of (P^1, {0,1,∞}); S_3 × Gal(C/R) symmetry

ideas.what: The fundamental groupoid of the thrice-punctured sphere with its symmetry group, as a 'preliminary exercise in Galois synthesis' towards Teichmüller groupoids.
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT action on π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}) with symmetric base points; Lego–Teichmüller game
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); developed by Drinfeld 1990, Ihara, Deligne 1989, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, Lego game, dihedral symmetric base points)

ideas.what: Compactifying Σ* to get base points 'close to' the punctures; on the next page this is the real oriented blow-up, with unit tangent circles as boundary.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points); Ihara; Anderson
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (base points 'à l'infini' / tangential, in spirit)

ideas.what: Planned generalizations: other highly symmetric configurations on the sphere, other surfaces, the sphere replaced by the Hopf fibration.
ideas.modern_name: Polyhedral/Platonic dessins and their automorphism groups; spin/framed versions of fundamental groupoids

missed.claim: Grothendieck suggests replacing the sphere by the Hopf fibration S^3 → S^2, i.e. lifting the Galois-synthesis exercise to a circle bundle over Σ*. S^3 is the spin double cover of the unit tangent bundle SO(3) of S^2. The next page's boundary circles are fibres of exactly this tangent circle bundle. Studying the fundamental groupoid of the Hopf/unit-tangent bundle over the punctured sphere, with its symmetries and Galois action, would amount to a 'framed' or 'spin' version of the Teichmüller-groupoid programme. That programme was not developed, as far as I know, in the anabelian/GT literature.
missed.quote: ou celle-ci étant remplacée par le fibré de Hopf
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Central extensions and framed/spin mapping class groups are now important (TQFT, theta characteristics, spin moduli). A GT/Galois action on framed or spin Teichmüller groupoids, built via Hopf-fibration base points, is a natural but little-explored extension.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly a routine set-up: symmetric coordinates for three points on the sphere, and the announcement of tangential base points, which are in the spirit of the Esquisse and later Deligne. The only mildly unexpected item is the passing programme of redoing the exercise for the Hopf fibration and for symmetric configurations on other surfaces. It is only listed, not developed.
transcription_corrections: Under the brace in (8): 'tout tel' should read 'tautol.' (tautologique).
In (8): '𝔤(𝔤) id_Δ' should read 'sg(g) id_Δ' (the sign of g), and the left side is g_E, the action of g on E, not a Lie algebra 𝔤.
Subscripts 'V_𝔍' should be 'V_J' (ordinary J), as on the previous page.
In (10): 'Σ ∖ 𝔍' is Σ ∖ J (the set of the R_j); the handwritten {R_i | i ∈ I} is Grothendieck's own index inconsistency.
Page number: '2' at top; folio '45' bottom left.
